title: Company-level Outcomes: Initiative Staging Map and Elastic Capacity Hedging
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a cross-functional playbook and visual staging map that ties company-level outcomes to a prioritized initiative slate and an 'elastic capacity hedge' policy. This artifact will be used by PM, Eng, and GTM to decide which initiatives are funded, staged, and can burst or pause depending on capacity and risk signals.
background: Recent quarters showed repeated overcommitment during peak infra demand and underinvestment against strategic bets. Current OKR boards lack a machine-readable staging layer for matching capacity scenarios to initiative releases. We need a pragmatic model that maps outcomes -> initiatives -> staging lanes with guardrails for elastic capacity (scale-up burst vs pause) and an escalation path.
goals: Produce a staging map that assigns each company-level OKR to a staging lane: Core, Accelerate, Experiment, or Hedge
Define a small set of capacity scenarios (baseline, peak, constrained) and the corresponding initiative actions (proceed, defer, pause, burst)
Ship a lightweight rubric and acceptance dashboard for leadership to make objective trade-offs during quarterly planning
acceptance_criteria: Staging map CSV published and ingested into OKR dashboard (Confluence + Looker link)
Policy doc for elastic capacity hedges endorsed by Eng, Infra, Finance, and PM leads
Two scenario walkthroughs run in planning dry-run with recorded decisions and roll-forward actions
Automated alerts wired from infra-cost and latency dashboards to trigger hedge recommendations
risks: Overly prescriptive hedging could stifle high-value experiments
Insufficient telemetry to evaluate scenario triggers accurately
Stakeholder buy-in may slip timeline if finance requests more modeling
decisions: Use 3 capacity scenarios (baseline, peak, constrained) scoped to token throughput and cost thresholds
Map initiatives into 4 lanes (Core, Accelerate, Experiment, Hedge) instead of binary go/no-go
Automated hedging recommendations remain advisory; final decision stays with initiative owner + exec sponsor
